_comment: XC-3 Phase 0b ledger of every src/app/api/**/route.ts that imports the RLS-bypassing service-role client (@/lib/supabase-admin or a relative path to lib/supabase-admin). This list RATCHETS DOWN ONLY: as Phase 2/3 migrate read routes onto the RLS-scoped supabase-server client, their entries are pruned here in the same PR. A NEW admin-importing route that is absent from this ledger FAILS src/__tests__/api-admin-client-allowlist.test.ts (which re-derives the detected set from source with the same import matcher). 263 -> 264: GenAI Phase 5a outcome-prediction cross-student read (service-role after canAccessStudent). 264 -> 265 (2026-07-29, architect-reviewed): P0-1 quota display/enforcement gap — src/app/api/usage/daily/route.ts reads the caller's OWN daily quota from get_plan_limit(), the SAME authority check_and_record_usage() enforces from. Service-role is REQUIRED here, not convenience: migration 20260729130400 §5 (re-asserting 20260516040000/20260516050000) REVOKEs EXECUTE ON public.get_plan_limit(uuid, text) FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, so an RLS-scoped session cannot call it at all. Bounded surface: one STABLE read-only RPC + one own-row SELECT on student_daily_usage, both keyed on the SESSION-derived auth.studentId (students.auth_user_id = caller) — no studentId is ever accepted from the request, so there is no cross-student path. Read-only: no insert/update/increment/grant; the hard gate stays checkAndIncrementQuota -> check_and_record_usage in /api/foxy. Gated by authorizeRequest() on 'foxy.chat'/'quiz.attempt' (both granted to the student role by 20260612123200); EVERY unrecognised ?feature= — inherited Object.prototype keys (toString/constructor/valueOf/hasOwnProperty/__proto__/isPrototypeOf/propertyIsEnumerable/toLocaleString) included — is rejected 400 BEFORE authorizeRequest and before any service-role call. Architect-verified against shipped source 2026-07-29: FEATURE_PERMISSION is a new Map<string, string> (route.ts:82-85) and the guard is typeof permission !== 'string' (route.ts:95-100); Map.prototype.get consults no prototype chain, so inherited keys are unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a guard each new call site must remember, and no caller-controlled string can reach get_plan_limit's generous ai_calls_total ELSE arm. HISTORY (CLOSED — recorded so the fix is not re-litigated, not as an open item): the pre-ship draft used a plain object literal typed Record<string, string>, where inherited keys returned truthy and slipped past the !permission guard. The impact was BROADER than first recorded here: a student caller got an unhandled 500 (rbac.ts:785 calls .split() on the non-string permission in the deny branch, above the try), but a super_admin caller took the isSuperAdmin short-circuit at rbac.ts:779-780, which skips the permission check entirely, so a prototype key DID reach get_plan_limit and land in its ai_calls_total ELSE arm. That path additionally required the caller to own a student row, and get_plan_limit is a read-only STABLE function, so the over-generous number was DISPLAY-only and never raised the ENFORCED cap in check_and_record_usage. Both paths are closed by the Map plus typeof guard, pinned by 4 tests covering 8 prototype keys. Response is 4 ints + 1 bool, no PII (P13). RATCHET-DOWN PATH: add an auth.uid()-anchored SECURITY DEFINER wrapper get_my_plan_limit(p_feature text) GRANTed to authenticated, move the route to the RLS-scoped client, and prune this entry. Do NOT instead GRANT EXECUTE on get_plan_limit(uuid, text) to authenticated — it takes p_student_id and performs no auth.uid() check, so that would expose every student's cap to every authenticated user. Pinned by REG-213 (P8/P9). 268 -> 269 (2026-08-02, architect-reviewed): Mock Exam Runner v2 autosave — new save-only route src/app/api/exams/papers/[id]/autosave/route.ts. Service-role is REQUIRED here, not convenience: mock_test_attempts RLS (20260520000008) keys mock_test_attempts_update_own/select_own on student_id = auth.uid() directly (student_id REFERENCES auth.users(id)), but this entire route family — this route's already-ledgered siblings [id]/start/route.ts and [id]/submit/route.ts (see 'Phase 2.2 mock-exam remediation' above) — resolves and filters on authorizeRequest()'s studentId, which is students.id, a DIFFERENT uuid than auth.uid(). An RLS-scoped client (supabase-server/supabase-route) filtering .eq('student_id', studentId) with that same studentId would be silently zero-rowed by the auth.uid()-keyed policy — indistinguishable from the route's own legitimate persisted:false no-op branch, i.e. a silent persistence failure, not a security win. Bounded surface: a single UPDATE scoped to id + student_id + exam_paper_id + status='in_progress', touching only the pre-existing client_metadata jsonb column — NEVER score_percent/raw_score/xp_earned/status/submitted_at (enforced by the route's own field-level write shape, not by a WHERE filter). Gated by the same exam.view authorizeRequest() permission as all three siblings; student_id/exam_paper_id/status are app-supplied filters only, never derived from a request-controlled join, so there is no cross-student read/write path. RATCHET-DOWN PATH: reconcile student_id semantics across the whole [id]/{start,submit,autosave} family (store auth.uid() consistently, matching the table's own RLS design, or add an auth.uid()-anchored SECURITY DEFINER autosave RPC mirroring submit_mock_test_attempt), then move all three routes to the RLS-scoped client together — flagged for architect/backend follow-up, out of scope for this PR. 269 -> 268 (2026-08-03, architect-approved in the P1 verifyCronAuth batch): src/app/api/cron/daily/route.ts DELETED — it was a deprecated alias for /api/cron/daily-cron, scheduled by nothing and carrying only deprecation telemetry; its entry is pruned in the SAME change so the ledger ratchets DOWN, not drifts. 268 -> 265 (2026-08-03, P2-7b): teacher/messages/{route,threads,threads/[id]/messages} migrated to SECURITY DEFINER RPCs under RLS (createSupabaseServerClient), pruned in the same change so the ledger ratchets DOWN. 268 -> 269 (2026-08-05, Foxy North-Star Phase 5 lane U10): NEW route src/app/api/v1/leaderboard/me/route.ts legitimately uses the admin client. Service-role read of the get_leaderboard_percentile RPC scoped to the SESSION-derived studentId (auth.uid()-resolved; ?student_id ignored) after authorizeRequest('leaderboard.view'); returns caller-owned percentile band + PII-free neighbours. Ratchet-down path: replace with an auth.uid()-anchored SECURITY DEFINER RPC then move to the RLS-scoped client. 269 -> 268 (2026-08-06, P1 health consolidation, commit eaa7e1ab): src/app/api/health/route.ts migrated to a pure-liveness endpoint (no downstream dependency probes, no service-role reads) and its ledger entry is pruned in the SAME change so the ledger ratchets DOWN, not drifts. 268 -> 269 (2026-08-11, architect-reviewed): Phase 4 quiz session resume — NEW route src/app/api/quiz/session/[sessionId]/progress/route.ts. RECORDED LATE, DELIBERATELY NOTED: the route landed in commit 6a67ca8ed without its ledger entry, so api-admin-client-allowlist.test.ts failed with 269 detected vs 268 pinned. The guard behaved exactly as designed — the omission was the author's, not the test's — and this entry closes it rather than relaxing the pin. Service-role is REQUIRED here, not convenience, and the reason is structural: public.quiz_session_shuffles has RLS ENABLED with exactly THREE policies and ALL THREE ARE 'FOR SELECT' — quiz_session_shuffles_student_select (student_id IN (SELECT students.id WHERE auth_user_id = auth.uid())), _parent_select (rewritten by 20260720170000) and _teacher_select. There is NO INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policy on the table at all, so under RLS every non-bypassing write is denied by default-deny; migration 20260814000020 then made that denial explicit at the privilege layer too (REVOKE ALL ON TABLE ... FROM PUBLIC/anon/authenticated, re-GRANT SELECT column-wise on the non-key columns only, asserted by its own post-condition 4d 'authenticated retains no write privilege'). An RLS-scoped client issuing this route's UPDATE would therefore be silently zero-rowed — indistinguishable from the route's legitimate first-write-wins 'saved:false' no-op branch, i.e. a silent durability failure, not a security win. ACL COMPATIBILITY (verified 2026-08-11): 20260814000020 revokes from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated ONLY and issues no REVOKE against service_role, so service_role keeps the baseline ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES table-level ALL — including UPDATE, and including UPDATE on the additively-added session_mode column (20260814000021), which inherits from that table-level grant. That migration's self-verifying block asserts service_role SELECT on the answer-key columns (4b) but never asserts service_role UPDATE; that is a post-condition COVERAGE gap, not a live defect, because no statement in either 000014 or 000015 can subtract a service_role privilege. A future migration that starts revoking from service_role must add the missing UPDATE assertion in the same change. Bounded surface: ONE table written (quiz_session_shuffles), ONE write verb (UPDATE), and reads limited to SELECT student_id (ownership probe), SELECT SHUFFLE_RESUME_COLUMNS (resume payload), plus two collateral reads — quiz_sessions.id filtered by student_id + idempotency_key (the already-submitted gate) and question_bank on QUESTION_BANK_RESUME_COLUMNS. The UPDATE sets ONLY student_selected_displayed_index, student_time_spent_seconds, student_answered_at (columns added by 20260802130000) and session_mode (20260814000021) — NEVER shuffle_map, options_snapshot, correct_answer_index_snapshot, integrity_hash or options_version_at_serve, and NEVER any row of quiz_sessions / quiz_responses / students / xp_transactions / any mastery table, so P1/P2/P4 scoring, XP and atomic submission remain exclusively submit_quiz_results_v2's job. Both read whitelists deliberately EXCLUDE correct_answer_index_snapshot and integrity_hash, so the answer key never leaves Postgres on this path even though the service-role client could read it — the route holds itself to the same column boundary 20260814000020 imposes on authenticated. Auth gate: BOTH verbs run requireOwnedSession() FIRST — authorizeRequest(request, 'quiz.attempt'); 403 'student_profile_required' when the session carries no students.id; then a probe of the session's owning student_id returning 404 'not_found' for an unknown session and 403 'forbidden' when owner !== the SESSION-derived studentId. No cross-student path: the only request-supplied identifiers are the sessionId path param and the questionId body field, both UUID-regex-validated, and no student id is EVER accepted from the request — the ownership comparison and the resume SELECT are both anchored to auth-derived studentId, so a caller can only reach rows whose student_id already equals their own. The write is additionally immutable-once-set via .is('student_selected_displayed_index', null) (first-write-wins, mirroring the identical replay lock in check_quiz_answer, so the two writers are safe in any interleaving), and per-question time is clamped to [0, MAX_QUESTION_SECONDS] before persisting so a resumed session cannot inflate past the P3 3s/question floor. P13: logs carry session/question UUIDs, booleans and counts only — never option text, correctness, or student-identifying data. RATCHET-DOWN PATH: add an auth.uid()-anchored SECURITY DEFINER RPC — persist_quiz_answer_progress(p_session_id uuid, p_question_id uuid, p_selected_displayed_index int, p_time_spent_seconds int, p_mode text) that re-resolves the caller's students.id from auth.uid(), repeats the ownership check and the IS NULL first-write-wins predicate INSIDE the function, and is GRANTed EXECUTE to authenticated (the same shape as the parent/teacher RPC sets in 20260803130000) — then move both verbs onto createSupabaseServerClient and prune this entry. The read half needs nothing new: quiz_session_shuffles_student_select and quiz_sessions_own (student_id = get_my_student_id(), i.e. students.id — the same uuid authorizeRequest returns, unlike the auth.uid()-keyed mock_test_attempts family above) already scope every row this GET reads, and question_bank is authenticated-readable, so the GET alone would work RLS-scoped today. It is the write, and ONLY the write, that pins this entry. Do NOT instead add a student UPDATE policy plus a table-level GRANT UPDATE on quiz_session_shuffles: 20260814000020's post-condition 4d exists precisely to keep authenticated write-less on this table, and a table-level grant would simultaneously reopen the in-flight answer-key column read that migration closed — if a write policy is ever added, the accompanying GRANT must be COLUMN-level and restricted to the four durability columns. Pinned by REG-213 (P8/P9). 269 -> 270 (2026-08-11, architect-reviewed): teacher worksheet answer key — NEW route src/app/api/teacher/worksheets/answer-key/route.ts, created expressly to UNBLOCK the question_bank answer-key column ACL. Service-role is REQUIRED here, not convenient, and the requirement is structural rather than incidental: public.question_bank.correct_answer_index is today SELECTable by every signed-in user for all ~12.8k rows, because students, parents and teachers all authenticate as the SAME `authenticated` Postgres role — so neither RLS nor a column ACL can distinguish 'teacher printing an answer key' (legitimate) from 'student reading the key mid-quiz' (the widest answer-key leak in the product). The pending ACL will REVOKE SELECT (correct_answer_index) ON question_bank FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, mirroring 20260814000020's treatment of the same column family on quiz_session_shuffles; at that point an RLS-scoped client (supabase-server/supabase-route, which runs as the caller's `authenticated` role) is denied the column BY CONSTRUCTION and this route cannot be written any other way. The single browser call site that previously read the column — apps/host/src/app/teacher/worksheets/page.tsx, `supabase.from('question_bank').select(… correct_answer_index …)` — is deleted in the SAME change and is the last blocker on that migration; no client code on this page selects the column any more. Bounded surface: ONE table (question_bank), ONE verb (SELECT), READ-ONLY — no insert/update/delete/RPC anywhere in the route — over exactly six columns (question_text, options, correct_answer_index, explanation, difficulty, bloom_level), filtered on subject + grade + is_active = true (+ optional difficulty), LIMITed to count*3 with count validated to an integer in [1,30], so the worst-case read is 90 rows of global CBSE content. question_bank carries no student_id, no school_id and no class_id, so there is no student row, no PII and no tenant data reachable on this path at all. Auth gate: authorizeRequest(request, 'worksheet.create') runs FIRST, above any parsing and any DB access — an EXISTING permission code (PERMISSIONS.WORKSHEET_CREATE in packages/lib/src/rbac.ts) already granted to the teacher role by 20260612123200_rbac_matrix_conformance.sql, so this change introduces NO new permission code and NO RBAC migration. It is also the narrowest already-granted code that names this exact capability; the broader class.manage used by the sibling /api/teacher/subjects would have worked but grants strictly more. No cross-tenant path: RBAC alone would say 'this role may build worksheets' without saying WHICH content, so a SECOND gate — resolveTeacherContentScope in ./_lib/worksheet-scope, the content-side analogue of canAccessStudent — restricts the read to (subject, grade) pairs the caller actually teaches. That scope is the UNION of teachers.subjects_taught/grades_taught (already the authority behind /api/teacher/subjects, i.e. this moves an existing CLIENT-side restriction to the server where it is a boundary rather than a hint) and the caller's ACTIVE class assignments, the latter resolved through the CANONICAL resolveTeacherIdentity + resolveTeacherRosterScope pair in @alfanumrik/lib/rbac rather than a fourth hand-rolled class_teachers/class_enrollments join (rbac.ts's 'Canonical Teacher Roster Resolution' section exists because three such copies drifted and lost their is_active filters). It fails closed on every axis: no ACTIVE teachers row -> 403 teacher_profile_required; empty union -> deny, never wildcard (an empty subjects_taught is explicitly NOT read as 'all subjects', which is the precise inversion this whole change closes); any lookup error throws and surfaces as a generic 500. Neither 403 body, nor the 400 validation bodies, nor the 500 body carries a question, an option or an answer index — the key is present ONLY in a 200 that cleared both gates. P5: grade is validated against VALID_GRADES as a STRING ('6'..'12'); an out-of-list value is rejected 400, never coerced. P13: logs carry subject, grade and set SIZES only — never teacher/student identity, never question or option text. RATCHET-DOWN PATH: after the ACL migration lands, add an auth.uid()-anchored SECURITY DEFINER RPC — get_worksheet_answer_key(p_subject text, p_grade text, p_count int, p_difficulty int) that re-resolves the caller's teachers.id from auth.uid(), repeats the subjects_taught/grades_taught + class-assignment scope check INSIDE the function (the same shape as the parent/teacher RPC sets in 20260803130000), and is GRANTed EXECUTE to authenticated — then move this route onto createSupabaseServerClient and prune this entry. Do NOT instead re-GRANT SELECT (correct_answer_index) to authenticated under a narrower RLS policy: RLS is row-scoped and the exposure here is COLUMN-scoped on rows that are legitimately world-readable, so no row predicate can express it. Pinned by REG-213 (P8/P9).
